In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of gene expression at the onset of transcription in early embryos.
determining whether a transient expression system can be used to study the regulation of transcription during early development.
understanding the mechanisms that control the onset of transcription during early embryogenesis in Xenopu laevis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the transformed Xenopus embryo is a useful transient expression system to determine the effects on gene expression of promoter strength, conformation of the injected DNA, degree of DNA replication, and regulatory molecules.
the MBT is not regulated at the level of transcriptional initiation but is regulated at the level(s) of transcriptional elongation, mRNA stability, or translation.
the MBT is a period during embryogenesis when transcriptional activity is initiated and not an absolute block to transcription.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MBT is not a general phenomenon, but is dependent on the injected DNA.

(1) the MBT is a time when transcriptional activity can be initiated in the Xenopus embryo and (2) the MBT may represent a time when a number of different factors (promoters, enhancers, etc.) can act to initiate transcription.
the MBT is not a transcriptional event per se.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transformed embryo at these early developmental stages is a good transient expression system for the analysis of gene expression at the MBT.
the MBT is a complex and highly regulated event, and that it is not simply a passive process of allowing transcription to occur.
we have established a new transient expression system that is simple, inexpensive, and easy to use.
